outcome: Reduction in niche width and depth
cohort: 35 patients with a uterine scar defect (niche) and the wish to conceive, who underwent robotic-assisted laparoscopic niche repair.
finding: Robotic-assisted laparoscopic niche repair (RALNR) significantly reduced niche width and depth, improved residual myometrial thickness, and resulted in a high subsequent pregnancy rate.
mod_finding: Seven re-cesarean sections were performed at term among the subsequent pregnancies.
followup_time: Initial assessment at 6 weeks post-surgery, with follow-up extending up to term for subsequent pregnancies.
